title: Ukrainian Frequency: word stress for every lemma of the top-12,000 list (over ukrainian-word-stress, en.wiktionary and uk.wiktionary)
abstract: A stressed form for each of the 12,000 lemma-and-part-of-speech rows of the Ukrainian Frequency list (v0.2.0, over UberText 2.0), keyed on the list's ranks: one confident stress where the open sources agree (9,674 of the 9,920 polysyllabic common words, 97.5 percent), a labeled free variant, homograph or dictionary-only doublet where they do not (225), and an honest `missing` for the 21 rows no source resolved. The 1,348 proper nouns are out of scope by owner decision: kept on their rows with the stress the pipeline found and the pipeline's status in the note, counted in no share. Every row carries the provenance of its stress; every manual decision is a ledgered override. Current release v1.0.0, CC-BY-SA 4.0 because of the Wiktionary-derived rows; kept as its own file rather than a column on the CC-BY list so the list is not relicensed. Reviewed snapshot of 2026-10-01 over list v0.2.0: ukrainian-word-stress 2.1.0 read directly from its trie and filtered by the list's UD part of speech, en.wiktionary (kaikki.org) and uk.wiktionary (dump) for doublets, a two-of-three vote, 19 goroh.pp.ua tiebreaks recorded as attested stress only, uk.wikipedia leads for 116 names, and a manual-decision ledger applied last. Joined on rank; kept as its own CC-BY-SA file so the CC-BY list is not relicensed. v1.0.1 (2026-10-07) corrects the credit for ukrainian-word-stress in the README and datasheet (a lang-uk project by Oleksiy Syvokon, maintained by Dmytro Chaplynskyi); the data files are byte-identical to v1.0.0. Datasheet, attribution and known defects: DATASHEET.md in this record. Checksums: manifest.json. Live page: https://www.jakelawrence.xyz/research/ukrainian-frequency.

title: A Deterministic Gate for Containing Prompt-Induced Unauthorized Record Updates (M-Anchor App V1)
abstract: M-Anchor App is a local Python application that separates AI-generated proposals from authoritative case-record updates. A deterministic gate checks the referenced state, externally admitted evidence, candidate transitions, and authority requests before saving a change. Its principle is: Model proposes; deterministic layer commits. The V1 demonstration includes four fixed attack types (unsupported resolution, forged evidence admission, future-check bypass, and state-reference tampering), two controls, an optional model connection, and separate English and Japanese documentation with a bilingual interface. Input, proposal, decision, and read-back state can be inspected and exported. The source package includes reproduction instructions, validation records, and two original observation exports containing 20 entries and one entry, respectively. The fixed observations show rejection of four invalid proposal types and acceptance of a supported update. Three model-route observations record one adversarial input that the model itself answered by preserving uncertainty, one valid no-change proposal, and one supported update saved from Version 1 to Version 2. The adversarial model example is not a gate rejection of an invalid model output. “Attack neutralization” is limited here to blocking unauthorized case-record transitions at the gate. The app does not prevent all incorrect GPT text, establish evidence truth, control external tools, or demonstrate universal prompt-injection or jailbreak resistance. This is a software demonstration with inspectable evidence, not an independently certified security product. Python 3.10 or later is required; fixed scenarios need no model API key. This distribution is licensed under Apache-2.0, permitting commercial use, modification, and redistribution under its terms. The M-Anchor Framework is a related, separately versioned project.

title: Whole-Path Hit Rates and Error in Sparse Range–Bearing Forecasting: research data, code and manuscript
abstract: Access update (1 October 2026): The authors have restricted file access for journal peer review. Record metadata and DOI remain public. Editors and reviewers may access the files using a private read-only link supplied separately through the journal submission system. This record was briefly publicly accessible before the restriction. Public-format correction: the manuscript and supplement now use a neutral standard LaTeX article layout. Scientific text, figures, tables, results and research evidence archive bytes are unchanged from v17-final (10.5281/zenodo.23073421). This version supersedes the template-formatted public documents. Research archive accompanying Whole-Path Hit Rates and Error in Sparse Range–Bearing Forecasting (v17-neutral), by Xu Zhang and Xianjian Zhang. The package includes the manuscript and supplement, multi-file LaTeX source, synthetic observations, model checkpoints, original evaluation records, observation-only replay, and separately labelled post-review extensions. Finite trajectory sets can favor different error and hit-rate objectives under sparse range–bearing sensing. We evaluate three learned model seeds on 6000 causal synthetic histories. Direct set-retention training reduces Top4 selection failure at 60 m by 1.66 percentage points relative to error-based ranking, but its mean-error effect depends on budget. Fixed-slot controls and a no-ID ablation limit interpretation as better per-history ranking. Analytic banks remain weaker than the learned eight-path bank. This is a bounded synthetic comparison, not real-platform validation or a deployment recommendation. Reproduction: original primary analyses and post-review extensions remain distinct. SHA-256 file manifests are included. Prediction replay was verified in a relocated directory using the recorded dependencies (Python 3.12, NumPy 2.5.3, PyTorch 2.14.0); fresh-install replication and independent full retraining have not been validated. Original training/selection role caches are not all duplicated and must be regenerated for full retraining. Author-only correspondence and review reports are excluded. Licensing: original code is MIT; original data, checkpoints, manuscript, supplementary material and archive documentation are CC BY 4.0. These licenses apply to different components, not as alternative licenses for every file. Third-party materials retain their existing licenses. No MDPI template is included in this version. See LICENSES.txt and LICENSE-MIT.txt inside the archive. This is a research archive, not an accepted journal publication. Download note: the v15 numerical-evidence ZIP and v16 review-extension ZIP are provided as 6 and 11 binary parts (at most 20 MiB each). Download all parts plus SPLIT_ARCHIVES.json and reassemble_archives.py to one directory and run python3 reassemble_archives.py. The standard-library-only script verifies each part and reconstructs the original ZIPs with SHA-256 checks. Other ZIPs are directly usable. See README_ARCHIVE.md for details.

title: Structural Barriers to the Deployment of AI Foundation Models
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) foundation models excel at benchmarks but are not always cost-effective or successfully deployed in enterprise systems. This paper analyzes the failures in their deployment through interconnected structural components characterized by: Economic constraints (computational costs, memory, and latency that scale with increasing use of AI model services), cognitive constraints (related to training objectives that optimize plausibility rather than causal reasoning and calibrated uncertainty), and socio-technical constraints (requirements for organizational change, accountability, and governance). The study examines why the deployment of AI models in real-world enterprise environments remains difficult. It focuses on four themes – scalability, reliability, interpretability, and practical deployment – aiming to demonstrate why these problems do not disappear even as models improve, and how these issues reinforce each other, thereby leading to higher costs and greater risk. In conclusion, the study outlines alternative development pathways, including the use of alternative architectural paradigms such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), hybrid Neuro-symbolic AI, compound and multi-agent systems, and human-in-the-loop designs, which may offer more practical and sustainable ways to align foundation models with the organizational, operational, and governance requirements of the enterprise environment. Additionally, a four-dimensional framework is proposed for assessing a model’s deployment readiness based on economic viability, reliability and safety, auditability, and organizational readiness.

title: DEEP NEURAL NETWORK-BASED SPEAKER AUTHENTICATION FOR SECURE ACCESS CONTROL SYSTEMS
abstract: In the digital age, the importance of biometric identification technologies is increasing due to the increasing demand for reliable, secure, and user-friendly access control systems for electronic devices. One of the promising areas of such technologies is speaker authentication, which allows confirming identity based on a person’s unique voice characteristics. However, traditional methods cannot provide the required level of stability in different acoustic environments, background noise conditions, and changes in speech features. In the presented research work, a comprehensive approach is proposed that combines multi-frequency coefficients (MFCCs), x-vector-based speaker inputs, and deep neural networks (DNNs) to improve the accuracy and stability of speaker authentication. The proposed architecture consists of preprocessing speech signals, extracting MFCC features, forming x-vector inputs, and classifying speakers using DNN. An experimental dataset consisting of audio recordings of 100 speakers was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model. As a result of the experiment, the proposed model achieved 98.5% authentication accuracy, 99.4% precision, 97.6% recall, and a 98.5% F1-score. In addition, the false acceptance rate (FAR) was 0.6%, the false rejection rate (FRR) was 2.4%, and the equal error rate (EER) was approximately 1.5%. These results indicate that the model can distinguish between authorized and unauthorized users with high accuracy. The proposed approach showed superior results compared to traditional machine learning and deep learning models, which proved the effectiveness of combining acoustic features and deep speaker embeddings. The results indicate that the proposed method can be used in secure access control to electronic devices, biometric user identification, and voice authentication systems.

title: Objects and Classes Will Do
abstract: Objects and classes were introduced by SIMULA some sixty years ago. Since then, many new language mechanisms have been devised including static members, namespaces, modules, companion objects, interfaces, mixins, traits, protocols, constructors, factories, iterators, etc. The implications are that many languages have become complex entities with many rules, special cases, and exceptions to the rules, often due to lack of uniformity and generality.

title: SKC-Net: A Standard-Cell Key-Feature Contrastive-Learning network for cervical abnormal cell detection
abstract: Deep learning-based detection of abnormal cells in cervical ThinPrep Cytology Test images represents a pivotal advancement in intelligent cervical cancer screening systems. In this context, the effective utilization of standard cell features in images is paramount.On one hand, the TBS diagnostic criteria delineate the differentiation based on feature comparisons between normal and abnormal cells. On the other hand, signiffcant inter-sample variations can lead to confusion during the learning process in conventional object detection networks. To mimic the diagnostic reasoning of professional pathologists, this paper introduces the Standard-Cell Key-Feature Contrastive-Learning Network for detecting cervical abnormal cells. The network initially extracts key features from both standard and abnormal cells and effectively aligns them using consistency-guided contrastive loss. To better distinguish the unique characteristics of standard and abnormal cells, we have designed a Multi-Color-Domain Convolution Module and an Adaptive Contour Approximation Module, which are based on TBS diagnostic criteria—focusing respectively on the preliminary extraction of color and shape features. Furthermore, to mitigate information loss during deep feature learning, we propose a Dual-Branch Differentiated Convolution Module aimed at enhancing the model’s learning capacity and memory retention. Finally, to guide the model’s learning process by leveraging standard cell key features, we introduce the Cell Instance-Level Contrastive Supervision Module; this enhancement signiffcantly boosts the overall model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves the mean Average Precision by 3.4% and 3.0% on the CLBC and CRIC datasets,respectively, achieving scores of 65.2% and 71.8%.These findings underscore the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

Furthermore, to mitigate information loss during deep feature learning, we propose a Dual-Branch Differentiated Convolution Module aimed at enhancing the model’s learning capacity and memory retention. Finally, to guide the model’s learning process by leveraging standard cell key features, we introduce the Cell Instance-Level Contrastive Supervision Module; this enhancement signiffcantly boosts the overall model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves the mean Average Precision by 3.4% and 3.0% on the CLBC and CRIC datasets,respectively, achieving scores of 65.2% and 71.8%.These findings underscore the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

title: Training datasets tailored for domain-specific large language models: challenges, methods and trends
abstract: Adapting LLMs to specialized domains critically depends on high-quality training data, making dataset construction a decisive factor in domain performance. This survey reviews methods for constructing domain-adaptation training datasets through a structured, data-centric analysis. Based on a comparative analysis of representative domain-specific LLMs, we organize the literature around three technical dimensions that address limited data availability, heterogeneous quality and inefficient utilization: data synthesis , data selection and data composition . For data synthesis, we examine paradigms based on instruction rewriting, unlabeled-corpus reconstruction, retrieval augmentation and knowledge-graph-guided generation. For data selection, we trace the progression from heuristic rule-based filtering to model-aware methods that estimate sample quality and training utility. Data composition encompasses mechanisms that control the effective training-data distribution by determining which data are used, how strongly different data contribute to optimization and when each data type is introduced. We further examine catastrophic forgetting during domain adaptation and summarize data-centric mitigation strategies based on replay, mixture design, data ordering and stage-wise allocation. Overall, this survey provides a systematic reference for constructing domain-adaptation training datasets and supports the transition of LLMs from general-purpose foundation models to domain-specialized systems.

title: Unifying Privacy Accounting: Information Equivalence and Information Loss
abstract: Differential privacy (DP) admits several notions, but the choice among them may affect both privacy analysis and utility. In this paper, we consider four mainstream curve-based privacy notions within a unified information-theoretic framework. For a fixed ordered pair of output distributions, we establish information equivalence among the two directional privacy profiles of $(\varepsilon,δ)$-DP, the pair of hypothesis-testing trade-off functions, and the extended privacy-loss distribution. The exact Rényi differential privacy (RDP) curve joins this equivalence class whenever it is finite at some order greater than one. Under this mild condition, choosing among these notions changes only their semantic interpretation and computational requirements. In contrast, taking the maximum of the directional privacy profiles or compressing the RDP curve into a single zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) parameter can lose information. We quantify the information loss between the exact RDP curve and its zCDP bound for standard noise mechanisms. This gap is zero for Gaussian noise but generally positive for Gaussian-mixture, Laplace, discrete Gaussian, and Poisson-subsampled Gaussian mechanisms. Moreover, this gap grows linearly with the number of independently composed mechanisms. Our information-theoretic perspective has practical consequences. At the same certified privacy level, retaining the full RDP curve rather than using zCDP reduces the required noise variance by up to $45\%$ for Gaussian-mixture noise in workloads comparable in size to the American Community Survey. For DP-SGD on Fashion-MNIST under Poisson subsampling, an RDP-based privacy accountant improves test accuracy by up to $8.73$ percentage points compared to a zCDP-based accountant when both are calibrated to the same $(\varepsilon,δ)$ guarantee.

title: Joint Movement and Compression Ratio Design for Mobile Embodied AI Networks (MEAN)
abstract: Mobile embodied AI networks (MEAN) enable embodied agents to perceive, reason, communicate, and act in wireless environments. In such networks, agent mobility can improve channel conditions, while semantic compression can reduce transmission payloads. However, movement consumes energy, and stronger compression incurs additional computational cost. This paper studies joint movement, semantic compression, and transmit power design for an uplink MEAN system. We formulate a max-min energy efficiency (EE) problem by jointly optimizing transmit power, movement distance, and semantic compression ratio under controllable power constraints. The problem is non-convex due to the coupled signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), mobility-dependent channel gains, and fractional EE objective. To solve it, we propose an alternating optimization (AO)-Dinkelbach algorithm, where the fractional objective is handled by the Dinkelbach transformation, transmit power is updated via successive convex approximation (SCA), and movement distance is updated by coordinate-wise grid search. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms no-mobility and no-compression baselines, demonstrating the benefit of jointly exploiting mobility control, semantic compression, and power allocation in MEAN.

title: SoK: Decentralized Agent Economic Infrastructure
abstract: Decentralized agent economies increasingly build a single task from protocols that were designed and secured separately. This creates a simple problem: a workflow can look correct at each step and still produce the wrong outcome. For example, a correct escrow may release payment on an authorized approval that provides little evidence that the delivered work actually satisfied the task. We systematize this problem across the full lifecycle of an agent task. Our study organizes security and economic requirements into 17 property families over six stages, with receipt soundness and completeness assessed separately. We examine 12 systems and standards, five reusable mechanism families, and four classical baselines. We introduce guarantee closure, a task-relative criterion for determining whether guarantees established at one stage remain available and constrain the later decisions that depend on them. We apply the criterion to controlled and native workflows, covering 840 matched executions and an exhaustive 11,648-case check over a finite objective-task domain. Our results expose recurring failures between verification and settlement, where conforming work can remain unaccepted or valid evidence can be ignored. Public records and model judgments further distinguish recorded approval from evidence of task conformance, while economic analysis identifies the report, penalty, and shared-error assumptions behind these guarantees. These findings show where end-to-end guarantees fail and what must be repaired to preserve them across the workflow.

title: Teaching LLMs to Hear Who Spoke What: Metadata-Supervised Pretraining for Encoder-Free Speech-LLMs
abstract: Encoder-based speech large language models (Speech-LLMs) commonly employ pretrained speech encoders that prioritize linguistic content but may discard fine-grained acoustic cues essential for speaker discrimination and paralinguistic understanding. Encoder-free Speech-LLMs instead map Mel-spectrogram features directly into the LLM input space through lightweight embedding layers, enabling the LLM to learn from low-level acoustic features. However, systematic pretraining strategies for encoder-free Speech-LLMs remain underexplored, limiting their ability to compensate for the absence of large-scale pretrained speech encoders. We propose metadata-supervised pretraining (MSP), which leverages speech attributes such as speaker identity and emotion to develop speaker-discriminative and paralinguistic capabilities. We further introduce speaker-aware utterance composition (SAUC) to strengthen speaker discrimination and apply random span masking to regularize pretraining. We primarily evaluate our approach on joint ASR and speaker diarization in multi-speaker conversations, complemented by experiments on paralinguistic speech-understanding tasks. Under matched training-data conditions, our encoder-free model outperforms its randomly initialized encoder-based counterpart. With limited metadata-annotated data, it is competitive with models using speech encoders pretrained on substantially larger corpora, outperforming them in several settings. These results demonstrate the potential of encoder-free architectures for building native multimodal LLMs that acquire diverse speech capabilities.

title: Efficient learning of quantum interactions from thermal metastable states
abstract: Learning quantum interactions from finite-temperature many-body systems is a central task in emerging quantum platforms. Recently, the problem of learning from lattice quantum Gibbs states has found rigorous, efficient protocols. Nevertheless, exact Gibbs states, as the input premise, are in fact computationally intractable to prepare and may not faithfully represent generic finite-temperature quantum systems. In contrast, a system coupled to a heat bath can be stuck at an approximate stationary state (metastable state) long before it truly equilibrates. Here, we formulate a physically and algorithmically consistent alternative: learning from such metastable states of detailed-balanced master equations (Lindbladians) arising from system-bath interactions. We distill the algorithmic mechanism and structural condition underlying Gibbs-state learning and extend it in full to metastable states, attaining nearly optimal sample and computational complexity (in the system size and the precision). More broadly, we sharpen notions of metastability and develop a unified framework for finite-temperature learning.

title: Zero- Versus Infinite-Temperature Damping in Variational Quantum Circuits: Feature Scale, Sampling Cost, and Frame Gauge
abstract: The Pauli twirl of amplitude damping (AD) is generalized amplitude damping at infinite temperature: it keeps the contraction of AD and removes its non-unital term, so comparing the two in variational circuits isolates the zero-temperature bias, which acts mainly through the scale of the features. For random parameters, features under AD settle on a floor, which at strong damping is set by the last layer, has a closed form, and at fixed $T_1$ falls with temperature as $\tanh(\hbarω/2k_BT)$; under the twirls they shrink by a constant factor per layer, up to eight qubits. A trainable output scale removes most of the resulting accuracy differences, leaving AD ahead of its twirls by at most about three percentage points in our simulations; what it removes reappears as a cost in measurement shots: trained and tested with $10^3$ shots per image, a four-qubit classifier under AD at $p=0.3$ stays within 1.5 points of noiseless accuracy, while the twirled classifiers lose up to 33. At weaker damping the separation depth grows roughly as $(np)^{-1}\ln(1/p)$. The damping direction is a gauge when the damping follows complete entangling layers and the circuit boundaries are trainable; in an eigensolver it becomes physical inside a decomposed two-qubit gate.

title: SLIM: Simplex-Lattice Interpolation Merging
abstract: Optimizing merging coefficients for large language models can require many costly benchmark evaluations. We propose \textbf{Simplex-Lattice Interpolation Merging (SLIM)}, which constructs a quadratic surrogate of aggregate performance on the coefficient simplex using a classical mixture design. Evaluations of individual experts and equal-weight pairs determine the surrogate with the minimum number of measurements needed to identify a general quadratic on this domain. SLIM then optimizes the surrogate without further target-metric evaluations. Experiments on two model architectures demonstrate accurate prediction of unseen multi-expert mixtures and competitive merge performance under limited evaluation budgets. Matched-budget comparisons show that structured evaluation points improve prediction fidelity over random designs, including those using regularized fitting.

title: Geometric Similarity in VLM Low-Level Vision Representations
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as powerful candidates for universal vision backbones, with representative architectures including autoregressive (AR) models and diffusion transformers (DiTs). Yet, adapting them efficiently for all-in-one low-level image restoration remains a challenge. Crucially, the field lacks an understanding of how VLMs organize hidden-layer representations and whether these structurally distinct paradigms share a common geometric organization for pixel-level perception. Such shared organization is a prerequisite for building highly transferable, unified restoration VLMs and adapters. In this paper, we systematically investigate representational similarity across 24 low-level tasks spanning 5 categories. We propose GeoSim, a unified four-level framework that analyzes task-conditioned representations from global similarity, local geometry, sparse feature decomposition, and topological verification perspectives. Our formulation applies to the analysis of hidden states in AR models and feature maps in DiTs across same- and cross-task/model settings. Our results reveal the organizing principles of low-level visual representations while exposing their limits in cross-task and cross-model agreement. Ultimately, GeoSim provides an interpretability lens for probing latent transferability in low-level vision and diagnosing model limitations in task- or model-specific scenarios.

title: Red-Teaming Coding Agents from a Tool-Invocation Perspective: An Empirical Security Assessment
abstract: Coding agents powered by large language models are becoming central modules of modern IDEs. They help users to perform various complex coding tasks by invoking tools. Although powerful, tool-invocation operation in coding agents opens a substantial attack surface for adversaries. Prior work has demonstrated attacks against both general-purpose LLM agents and domain-specific agents. However, to our knowledge, no previous works focus on the security risks of tool-invocation in coding agents. To fill this gap, we conduct the first systematic, in-depth red-teaming from a tool-invocation perspective in six popular real-world coding agents: Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline, and Trae. Our red-teaming proceeds in two phases. In Phase 1, we conduct a prompt leakage as reconnaissance to recover system prompts and related context. Specifically, we identify a mode gap between chat generation and tool-call argument generation: during schema-driven argument completion, the model behaves as if it is performing benign structured filling and may copy hidden agent context into tool-call arguments. We instantiate this gap as ToolLeak, which exfiltrates agent-internal prompts (e.g., system prompts and tool metadata) via required tool parameters. In Phase 2, we hijack the tool-invocation behavior of the coding agent with a novel two-channel prompt injection in the tool description and the tool return. Our hijacking achieves remote code execution (RCE) on major real-world coding agents. We adaptively construct the malicious payload using leaked security information in Phase 1. Our evaluation shows that ToolLeak substantially outperforms strong prompt-leak baselines in both emulated and real-world settings. In the emulated setting, ToolLeak achieves the best overall prompt-exfiltration performance across all six simulated coding agents. On real-world coding agents, ToolLeak achieves the best pseudo-recall on 18 of 25 evaluated agent-LLM pairs. Furthermore, our red-teaming successfully hijacks all six real-world coding agents for RCE and consistently yields higher attack success rates than baseline attacks. Lastly, we present two case studies on Cursor and Claude Code to demonstrate the real-world impact of our red-teaming.

title: Codec-induced Mismatch, Speech Duration, and Speaker-dependent Effect in a DNN-based Forensic Speaker Recognition System
abstract: The performance of forensic automatic speaker recognition (FASR) systems under the combined effects of codec-induced mismatch and different questioned-speech (QS) durations remains insufficiently understood, particularly at the individual speaker level.This study investigates the combined impact of representative lossy speech codecs (G.711 A-law, AMR-NB, and Opus) and QS duration on a DNN (ResNet34-MHA)based FASR system.System-level performance was generally good across all codec conditions, especially with >30s speech.Codec effects vary, however, with low-bitrate AMR-NB causing the greatest degradation in performance and Opus having minimal impact.Crucially, individual-level analyses reveal substantial speaker-dependent variability that is obscured by systemlevel metrics: some speakers exhibit persistently poor or unstable performance, and speakers with poorer overall performance are more sensitive to codec-induced mismatch.These findings demonstrate that promising system-level performance does not guarantee good performance for all speakers and highlights the need for individual-level analysis when testing DNNbased FASR systems.

title: We Do Care Global — Published Projects Portal & Autonomous AI Governance OS
abstract: Author portal and open-source portfolio for We Do Care Global, founded by Emir Perla in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The organization operates on a fundamental pledge of dedicating 33% of its annual revenue to provide financial and material assistance to vulnerable individuals worldwide for a dignified life. In technology, We Do Care Global delivers autonomous AI governance from first principles across 6 core systems: multi-agent factory orchestration (FoundationCentar), agent security and policy control planes (AgentGuard), enterprise function calling and secrets governance (AgentVault), production retrieval-augmented generation (Enterprise Hybrid-RAG with NVIDIA NeMo), agent observability and benchmarking (Agent Eval), and pharmacovigilance intelligence (Pharma Intelligence OS). Every release is archived on Zenodo with permanent DataCite DOIs under Apache-2.0 and attributed to ORCID 0009-0009-8515-2727.

title: Membership and Fraternal Ontologies
abstract: First release of two layered OWL 2 DL + SKOS ontologies for describing membership organisations as Linked Open Data. Membership Organisations (https://w3id.org/membership, prefixes mbr: and mbrc:): membership organisations of every kind, closed or open: clubs, societies, student nations, associations, political parties and trade unions. Membership lifecycle, admission and fees, offices and terms, gatherings, distinctions and conferrals, premises, reciprocity, catalogue facts. title: Comparing Fairness Methods for ICU Risk Prediction in MIMIC-IV
abstract: Fairness has become a critical component of responsible machine learning, particularly as models are increasingly deployed in clinical settings. While mitigating bias is essential, maintaining predictive performance remains a key challenge. Fairness-Aware Interpretable Modeling (FAIM) [1] is an in-processing method designed to improve fairness without significantly degrading performance and preserving model interpretability. In this study, we evaluate the robustness of FAIM by applying it to a substantially different clinical prediction task than originally proposed. Specifically, we shift from hospital admission prediction following emergency department (ED) stay to predicting the need for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, using electronic health record (EHR) data from the MIMIC-IV database. We compare FAIM against a baseline logistic regression model and several state-of-the-art fairness methods. Results indicate that, although disparities across intersectional demographic subgroups are not fully eliminated, FAIM consistently improves fairness relative to both the baseline model and other fairness approaches, while maintaining competitive predictive performance.

title: Application of hybrid neuro-fuzzy models to the inverse problem of chemical kinetics
abstract: Hybrid neuro-fuzzy models provide a tool for identifying hidden patterns in data and are based on nonclassical mathematical methods collectively known as soft computing. Soft computing has no rigorous axiomatic foundation and relies on heuristic algorithms; its methods have no strictly defined boundaries and include artificial neural networks, fuzzy logic, evolutionary algorithms, and other approaches. The mathematical justification for these methods rests on rigorously proven statements: any nonlinear system can be approximated by an artificial neural network (a multilayer perceptron) with two hidden layers, while any mathematical system can likewise be approximated by a fuzzy logic structure using if–then rules and fuzzy algebra operations. A hybrid model combines the advantages of the two approaches. During hybrid learning, the parameters of the membership functions are optimized and subsequently processed according to the rules of fuzzy algebra. Neuro-fuzzy models can be trained rapidly, provide good approximation (interpolation) accuracy, and are widely used in adaptive process control systems. This paper presents examples of hybrid kinetic models developed for a model chemical reaction between two reactants and for the gas-phase hydrochlorination of acetylene in a flow-recirculation system. The model results are presented in tabular form and visualized as response-surface plots. The corresponding crisp kinetic models were derived in the form of regression equations, which were then used to propose reaction mechanisms consistent with these equations.

title: Projeto Urna - Transparente Integridade dos dados eleitorais no Brasil em 2026
abstract: Este projeto tem como objeto a integridade dos dados eleitorais das eleições gerais de 2026 no Brasil, tomando como recorte as eleições para Presidente da República e para os governos estaduais. O principal objetivo é medir a integridade dos dados eleitorais brasileiros, incorporando análises forenses dos resultados ao relatório de observação eleitoral da Transparência Eleitoral Brasil e ampliando, assim, a verificação do sistema eletrônico de votação e o controle social do processo eleitoral. O problema que motiva a pesquisa é a desconfiança de parte considerável do eleitorado brasileiro em relação ao sistema eletrônico de votação, decorrente em parte da ausência de um comprovante de votação paralelo verificado pelo eleitor (voter-verified paper audit trail, VVPAT). Pesquisa Genial/Quaest de fevereiro de 2026 indica que 43% da população desconfia do sistema de votação, proporção que chega a 69% entre eleitores de Jair Bolsonaro — que obteve 49,10% dos votos na eleição presidencial de 2022 — e a 22% entre eleitores de Lula. O sistema brasileiro é de registro direto do voto (Direct Recording Electronic, DRE) sem VVPAT. Uma consequência central desse desenho é que a integridade do funcionamento do sistema e do resultado depende inteiramente da integridade do software; sem registro paralelo do voto em papel, as auditorias do software e do sistema como um todo são a principal maneira de a cidadania atestar a integridade da urna eletrônica. Daí a pergunta que organiza o projeto: como medir a integridade do sistema eleitoral de forma mais objetiva, para além de indicadores baseados em percepção, que dependem de avaliações subjetivas, são influenciados por fatores contextuais e podem divergir do que efetivamente ocorre na prática? Objetivos específicos. (i) Aplicar métodos estatísticos voltados à análise da integridade de dados eleitorais, contemplando testes baseados na distribuição de dígitos e na ocorrência de percentuais inteiros; (ii) aplicar rotinas computacionais para identificar padrões anômalos em resultados eleitorais, com foco na distribuição dos votos válidos e na taxa de comparecimento; (iii) analisar a consistência dos resultados eleitorais por meio da comparação entre diferentes estratégias de detecção de anomalias, de modo a verificar a robustez dos achados e ampliar a transparência da análise. A pesquisa utilizará dados públicos disponibilizados pelo Repositório de Dados Eleitorais do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). A unidade de análise principal será a seção eleitoral, podendo também ser empregados dados agregados por zona e por município para fins de comparação e testes de robustez. Serão aplicadas, de forma combinada, diferentes técnicas de estatística forense eleitoral, organizadas em três eixos: (1) análise da distribuição dos dígitos dos votos recebidos pelos candidatos — segundo dígito significativo (2BL), média do último dígito (LD) e frequência relativa dos dígitos finais 0 e 5; (2) exame da relação entre a proporção de votos obtidos pelas candidaturas e a taxa de comparecimento eleitoral, por meio de gráficos de dispersão e histogramas bidimensionais (fingerprint plots, FPP); e (3) análise da distribuição das proporções de votos válidos, com técnicas não paramétricas de densidade Kernel reamostrada (RKD), para identificar concentrações incomuns em percentuais arredondados ou inteiros, como 50%, 60%, 65% ou 70%, compatíveis com processos artificiais de fabricação ou ajuste dos resultados (Rozenas, 2017). O conjunto será complementado pelo modelo eforensics, que emprega uma estrutura de mistura finita separando os dados em três situações possíveis — ausência de fraude, fraude incremental e fraude extrema — e informa a probabilidade de fraude extrema e incremental, além da quantidade de votos manipulados. Todas as análises serão implementadas no software R, com scripts replicáveis para limpeza dos dados, construção dos indicadores, aplicação dos testes estatísticos e produção das visualizações. Sempre que possível, serão utilizadas rotinas abertas e pacotes já consolidados na literatura de estatística forense eleitoral. O projeto adota procedimentos de transparência e reprodutibilidade: o desenho é pré-registrado no Open Science Framework e todos os materiais necessários à replicação, incluindo bases de dados originais e scripts computacionais, serão disponibilizados publicamente, de modo que qualquer pessoa possa corroborar ou refutar os resultados de forma independente. A interpretação dos resultados será feita de forma integrada. Nenhum teste isolado será tratado como prova definitiva de fraude ou de ausência de fraude. Em vez disso, a pesquisa avaliará a convergência entre diferentes indicadores estatísticos: a presença simultânea de anomalias em múltiplas técnicas aumentaria a plausibilidade de irregularidades, enquanto a consistência dos resultados com os parâmetros esperados reforçaria a hipótese de integridade da contagem. Na ausência de fraude, os parâmetros de referência adotados são: 4,187 para a distribuição do segundo dígito conforme a Lei de Benford; 4,5 para a média do último dígito; 0,2 para a frequência dos números 0 e 5 como último dígito; correlação igual a 0 e não estatisticamente significativa entre taxa de comparecimento e percentual de votos válidos do candidato vencedor; e 0,07 para a densidade reamossada de Kernel da proporção de votos válidos (valor observado no Canadá). Espera-se que os resultados contribuam para o fortalecimento da confiança pública nas eleições brasileiras, ao oferecer uma avaliação técnica, independente e replicável da qualidade dos dados eleitorais. Os produtos previstos incluem uma ferramenta computacional desenvolvida especificamente para a detecção de anomalias estatísticas em dados eleitorais (pacote de R), submetida a validação independente, a realização dos testes de integridade imediatamente após a divulgação dos resultados oficiais e a divulgação pública de um relatório final de atividades, acompanhada de apresentação pública dos resultados.

title: Artificial intelligence in cervical cancer immunology: A review of mechanisms and clinical applications
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a significant global health burden, with its pathogenesis closely linked to persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and immune evasion mechanisms. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in oncology, particularly in immunology research, offering novel insights into disease mechanisms and enhancing clinical decision-making. This review systematically summarizes the latest advances in AI-driven research and applications in CC immunology. By integrating multi-omics data, AI enables high-resolution profiling of the tumor immune microenvironment and facilitates the identification of key biomarkers and signaling pathways. In clinical settings, AI has significantly improved the accuracy and efficiency of CC screening, diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognosis prediction. Despite persistent challenges such as data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and the need for prospective validation, the convergence of AI and immunology is paving the way for more precise and personalized management of CC. This review underscores the translational potential of AI in immunology and highlights its role in advancing the global effort to eliminate CC.

title: Predicting electric-field noise in ion traps using fluctuation electrodynamics
abstract: Electric-field noise in microfabricated surface ion traps contributes to gate errors in trapped-ion quantum computers, but this noise has been challenging to predict. Here, we present a method to predict the electric-field noise arising from fluctuations in the bulk of dielectric and metallic materials. The method is valid for arbitrary trap geometries, and the only relevant material property is energy loss. We apply it to an ion trap with an electrically floating electrode and find the contribution from dielectrics to be dominant. Our model predicts the observed noise for this trap within a factor of four. In addition, we apply our model to typical surface trap designs and analyze how the electrode structures shield the noise.

title: OpenMTB-Audit: Exposing Over-Refusal and Clinical Expert Perspectives in LLM-Based Molecular Tumor Board Safety Evaluation
abstract: Molecular tumor boards integrate genomic findings, clinical context, and therapeutic evidence to support precision oncology. As AI enters this workflow, a key safety challenge is distinguishing truly unsupported recommendations from evidence-supported options that still require oncologist review because of incomplete information, poor ECOG performance status, or other clinical caveats. We introduce OpenMTB-Audit, an open-source benchmark of 500 synthetic non-small cell lung cancer cases spanning five adversarial error categories and four safety labels: Supported, Partially Supported, Unsupported, and Insufficient Information. Across eight large language model configurations, we identify pervasive over-refusal: all LLM configurations failed to retain the Partially Supported label in 83.3-100% of true Partially Supported cases, achieving high aggregate safety scores through label collapse rather than clinically calibrated reasoning. To address this limitation, we developed MTB-AuditAgent, a deterministic seven-module framework separating evidence verification, missing-information detection, safety classification, and abstention. It reduces over-refusal to 6.7% and achieves 91.2% accuracy (95% CI: 88.6-93.6%). A two-oncologist annotation study found disagreement concentrated at the boundary between information sufficiency and treatment optimization, underscoring the need to preserve clinically meaningful distinctions.

title: DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents
abstract: Errors in LLM agent executions and their visible consequences can be separated by many steps, making decisive-error localization a matter of understanding both step content and step dependencies. We introduce DeFA, a dependency-guided framework for agent failure attribution. DeFA first combines protocol relations and semantic dependencies into an event dependency graph spanning the trajectory. It then identifies events that may violate task requirements and traces their sources and subsequent effects to construct a failure propagation graph. Finally, DeFA uses step evidence and the steps' roles in failure propagation to identify the decisive error, responsible agent, and error category. To support long trajectories, DeFA partitions executions into segments and combines the current segment's detailed content with summaries of the other segments, giving local diagnosis access to global execution context. Across Who and When and the Who and When Pro text subset, DeFA achieves the highest responsible-agent and exact step accuracy with all evaluated backbones, and the highest failure-mode accuracy among taxonomy-aligned methods on Pro. Further experiments on image and video trajectories demonstrate its applicability to multimodal failure attribution. Ablations support the contributions of segmentation, the event dependency graph, and the failure propagation graph. Using DeFA's diagnostic feedback for skill evolution in Trace2Skill improves downstream task accuracy by 6-15 percentage points over the native pipeline, showing that the diagnoses can also support agent improvement on subsequent tasks.

title: Posterior sampling by source-space MCMC via prior-based few-step transport maps
abstract: Bayesian inference increasingly uses informative but implicit priors represented only by samples, such as historical ensembles, simulator outputs, and pretrained generative models. The same computational problem appears in the test-time guidance task (generalized Bayes), where an explicit positive weight, e.g., an exponentiated reward, tilts an implicit prior. We develop a framework for source-space generalized Bayesian inference that combines inexpensive few-step prior transports with posterior stability guarantees. Specifically, we represent the prior using a one- or few-step improved MeanFlow (iMF) map and perform posterior sampling in its Gaussian source space. We establish Wasserstein error bounds between the exact and learned posteriors in terms of the joint population iMF and auxiliary-velocity loss, decomposed into training suboptimality and model-class approximation error. In the iMF source space, we adopt parallel tempering with preconditioned Crank-Nicolson updates and introduce a hybrid variant that incorporates split Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to improve sampling efficiency. Synthetic experiments show that the proposed framework can approximate posterior distributions accurately and efficiently, while CLIP-guided ImageNet experiments demonstrate its ability to steer a pretrained iMF image prior toward text-specified preferences.

title: A multiset approach to MacWilliams identities
abstract: Abstract We interpret the symmetrized weight enumerator of linear codes over finite commutative Frobenius rings as a summation over multisets and thereby provide a new proof of the MacWilliams identity for the symmetrized weight enumerator. The proof and the identity are expressed in combinatorial terms that do not require generating characters. We also generalize the symmetrized weight enumerator with respect to supports and codeword tuples, and our multiset approach enables us to derive new and general MacWilliams identities expressed in combinatorial terms.

title: Evolving Attention: Automated Discovery of a Competitive, Query-less Attention Mechanism
abstract: The attention mechanism is a cornerstone of modern deep learning, yet its canonical scaled dot-product form was the result of human design. This work explores the automated discovery of novel attention mechanisms from a space of fundamental mathematical primitives. We present a system that co-evolves both the computational graph of an attention formula and its associated linear projection strategy using the NSGA-II multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. A primary challenge in this expressive search space is the prevalence of semantically invalid "cheater" architectures. We introduce a definitive, path-aware semantic validator that enforces the logical ‘Score -> Normalize -> Aggregate‘ data flow, drastically improving search efficiency and the quality of discovered candidates. Our system successfully converged on a novel, query-less attention mechanism where attention scores are derived from a ‘Value-Key‘ interaction. The co-evolutionary search also determined its optimal projection configuration, disabling the standard query and key layers. In a multi-modal benchmark, this discovered mechanism achieved highly competitive performance, yielding 57.21% accuracy on CIFAR-10 (vs. 59.08% baseline) and 50.04% on IMDB (vs. 51.35% baseline), proving its viability as a general-purpose, automatically-discovered AI component with a fundamentally different operational logic.

title: Motor Matemático de Criptografia Simétrica de Preservação de Formato (FPE)
abstract: O presente programa de computador consiste em um motor de criptografia simétrica projetado para garantir a confidencialidade de dados numéricos em sistemas de informação, bancos de dados e tráfego de redes. O objetivo central da aplicação é implementar a técnica de Preservação de Formato (Format-Preserving Encryption - FPE). A arquitetura computacional permite que uma cadeia numérica de entrada (texto em claro) seja processada e transformada em um criptograma numérico de exata equivalência dimensional. Dessa forma, o software garante que sistemas legados e modelos de banco de dados restritos possam armazenar dados cifrados sem a necessidade de alteração de suas tipologias de infraestrutura (por exemplo, um dado numérico de 11 dígitos resultará, após o processamento, em um criptograma numérico também de 11 dígitos). O sistema é bidirecional, provendo tanto a rotina de cifragem quanto a de decifragem mediante autorização sistêmica.

title: Architectural Style as Evidence
abstract: Listing copy names architectural styles loosely, and a single label such as "Craftsman Bungalow" conflates what a house is with how it is shaped and what it is decorated with. This article describes an ontology, written in Prolog, that records a house's architectural character on four separate axes: movement, style, form and detail. It covers the styles common in California, from the Victorian family through Period Revival, the Spanish-derived group, the modern line and post-war vernacular. The ontology keeps association apart from entailment. Only one relation, a style expressing a movement, licenses inference; typical forms, typical details and routine confusions are recorded as evidence that nothing is inferred from. Details observed by a person can be weighed against the styles that could explain them, with each detail's weight computed from how many styles claim it rather than fitted, so the division of evidence can be shown and defended in a report. The article also sets out the guards that stop style words modifying something other than the house, such as "Craftsman quality" or "Tudor Drive", from asserting a style, and records the known limits and contested points of the classification.

title: Formalising Intentional Policy Graphs as Directed Multi-Graphs for Teleological Explanations
abstract: The use of Policy Graphs and their intentional version for doing Explainable Agency is an interesting tool for the Agents community. These models provide convenient and easy ways to build telic explanations of the function of agents’ actions. However, the definitions and algorithms presented thus far leave many ambiguities in their interpretation, and desires – a key component of these models – are not generalised and sometimes require ad-hoc programming. In this work, Intentional Policy Graphs are reintroduced with a brand-new notation (based on Directed Multi-Graphs) that solves these problems, and generalises the concept of desire. Furthermore, under the new notation, it provides two algorithmic optimisations for computing intentions.

title: Sensor Placement Optimization for Cooperative Active Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems
abstract: Abstract Effective perception in multi-robot systems depends both on the physical placement of sensors and on their active control during operation. However, existing approaches typically address sensor placement and active sensing separately, neglecting the dependency between hardware configuration and sensing strategies. In this work, we propose a two-stage framework for cooperative active sensing in robot teams equipped with multiple steerable sensors. In the first stage, sensor placement and base orientations are optimized using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) multi-objective genetic algorithm, balancing field-of-view overlap and angular sensing density under platform constraints. In the second stage, cooperative sensor control is formulated as a reinforcement learning problem. Centralized policies trained with three algorithms—Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)—learn to rotate sensors within bounded ranges around the optimized orientations to maximize environmental coverage while maintaining visual observation of teammates, with SAC achieving the highest reward improvement of up to 11.5%. Simulation experiments with teams of three robots show that the proposed approach significantly improves sensing coverage compared to static configurations, demonstrating the benefit of jointly considering sensor placement and cooperative active sensing.

title: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation with sentiment-aware responses for depression
abstract: In view of the rapid growth in conversational interfaces, there is a demand for more adaptive retrieval systems. Traditional chatbots, built on pre-trained models, struggle to understand and respond to a wide range of real-world user queries. In view of this, a framework based on multimodal retrieval-augmented generation with sentiment-aware responses (MRAG-SAR) for depression that addresses the challenges and strengthens conversational interface performance has been developed. The proposed system can process unstructured data in multiple formats of inputs, such as audio, image, and text, using a multimodal late-fusion mechanism, making it suitable for managing diverse, domain-specific information. It also leverages powerful embedding models for capturing contextual similarity and scalable vector databases for efficient retrieval. The user queries are augmented to provide precise and nuanced context-related responses. The proposed framework retrieves content that captures the dimensions of the topic to enhance the relevance of the output responses. Introduction of sentiment-aware response generation allows the system to respond in a tone based on the emotional context of the user queries, which is essential in making use of personalized conversations. Relevant bidirectional encoder representations from transformers score (BERTScore) and other metrics highlight the framework's effectiveness in delivering high-quality responses.

title: Towards Scalable and Verifiable Automated Translation from C to Safe Rust
abstract: Memory-safety bugs are one of the oldest and most common sources of security vulnerabilities, and their modern-day prevalence is a consequence of the widespread use of non-memory-safe languages such as C and C++. Transitioning away from C and C++ to memory-safe languages, namely Rust, to eliminate memory-safety bugs is growing in popularity as a potential solution, but manual migration of the vast C/C++ codebases in deployment to Rust is hardly practical.

title: Robust knowledge tracing via bidirectional context and conditional diffusion
abstract: Abstract Knowledge Tracing (KT) is essential in online education for modeling learners’ evolving knowledge states to support personalized instruction. However, conventional KT approaches often exhibit instability when confronted with abrupt shifts in learner performance—such as sudden errors amid consistent success or unexpected recoveries after prolonged failure. These non-stationary response patterns challenge models that rely on local sequential updates, leading to overreaction, delayed adaptation, or inconsistent predictions. To address this, we propose DiffKT , a knowledge tracing framework that enhances robustness through holistic sequence modeling. DiffKT first introduces a Bidirectional Global Context-aware State Estimator (GCSE), which leverages the full interaction sequence—past and future—to construct stable, context-rich representations of latent knowledge states, thereby mitigating myopic bias. Building on these representations, DiffKT employs a conditional diffusion process to iteratively refine knowledge state estimates by denoising corrupted sequence-level proxies. This enables the model to distinguish transient anomalies from genuine learning signals and maintain temporal consistency across dynamic response patterns. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets show that DiffKT achieves competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in next-response prediction. Further case studies and ablation analyses confirm that the integration of bidirectional context and diffusion-based refinement jointly improves robustness to abrupt performance shifts and generalization across diverse learning trajectories.

title: GallinaC: Unifying Verification and Certified Compilation of System Programs in Rocq
abstract: Systems programming demands strong correctness guarantees, yet verification remains challenging due to low-level memory manipulation and the gap between source-level reasoning and compiled code. We present GallinaC , a framework that unifies verification and certified compilation of system programs. GallinaC is a shallow, monadic embedding of a C-like language into Gallina, the specification language of the Rocq Prover. This enables programs to be written and verified directly in a single setting, without introducing a separate syntactic representation. We equip GallinaC with a separation logic expressed in Gallina, supporting modular reasoning about memory and stateful computations. To connect reasoning with execution, we define both denotational and operational semantics and prove their agreement. We build a certified compilation pipeline on top of CompCert, ensuring that verified properties are preserved down to executable code. By integrating programming, verification, and compilation, GallinaC reduces the gap between code and proofs and enables source-level optimizations, including a more exhaustive tail call optimization than CompCert’s.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastric Cancer: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Predictive Developments, Evidence Maturity, and Translational Challenges
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden characterized by substantial heterogeneity in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has been increasingly investigated for the analysis of endoscopic images, radiological scans, whole-slide pathology images, molecular profiles, liquid-biopsy data, and multimodal clinical datasets. This structured review summarizes recent AI-based developments in GC diagnosis, staging, prognostic assessment, and treatment-response prediction, with particular emphasis on the translational maturity of the available evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant English-language publications from database inception through January 2026. Eligible studies were evaluated according to clinical task, data modality, model type, cohort size, study design, validation strategy, interpretability, clinical workflow readiness, and reported limitations. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent AI models have demonstrated promising performance in selected research settings, particularly in endoscopic image analysis, computational pathology, CT-based radiomics, and multimodal prognostic modeling. However, most studies remain retrospective, single-center, and internally validated. Calibration, robustness, prospective clinical utility, and generalizability across populations and institutions remain insufficiently assessed. Major barriers to translation include data heterogeneity, annotation variability, overfitting, data leakage, external validation failure, algorithmic bias, regulatory requirements, reimbursement, clinician-AI interaction, medicolegal responsibility, post-deployment monitoring, and model drift. CONCLUSION: AI has considerable potential to support GC diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning, but most current models remain insufficiently validated for routine clinical use. Future progress will depend on transparent reporting, standardized validation, multicenter prospective trials, clinically meaningful endpoints, and the integration of explainable, trustworthy AI systems into routine clinical workflows.

title: Heteroclinic cycles and long-time behavior in a singularly perturbed three-species Lotka--Volterra system
abstract: We study a three-species competitive Lotka--Volterra system with cyclic dominance, motivated by rock--paper--scissors interactions in ecological communities. The model contains a singularly strong interaction coefficient of order 1/ε, representing a regime in which one species exerts a much stronger competitive pressure on another. We show that, despite this strong asymmetry, the cyclic dominance mechanism persists. Our main result is a quantitative description of one complete dominance pattern in the singular regime 0<εll 1. Starting near the state where the third species dominates, we prove that the solution successively passes near the dominance states of the second and first species before returning to a comparable configuration. We obtain logarithmic estimates for the return time and for the population densities at the return section. In particular, although one species becomes extremely small at the beginning and at the end of each pattern, it recovers to an order-one density during the cycle. We then prove that this pattern repeats indefinitely and that the omega-limit set is composed of three heteroclinic orbits on the boundary of the positive orthant, connecting the three single-species equilibria. Thus the long-time behavior is cyclic but aperiodic, with increasingly long excursions near successive single-species states.

title: Evidence-Gated Research: Statistically Controlled Model Adoption in Adaptive Search
abstract: Adaptive model search is path dependent: once a challenger is adopted, it becomes the reference from which later candidates are generated. A statistically unsupported replacement can therefore alter hypotheses that have not yet been proposed. We introduce Evidence-Gated Research (EGR), a statistical adoption layer for moving-incumbent search. EGR freezes each challenger before decision evidence is revealed, builds anytime-valid evidence across a predeclared set of environments, routes evidence predictably toward unresolved components, composes a persistent candidate e-value, and passes that e-value to an online controller. Under explicit conditional-validity and predictability conditions, the resulting procedure controls false discovery rate for the declared all-environment adoption target even though earlier adoptions change later challengers. In a 5,000-trajectory closed-loop benchmark, development-only e-LOND attains persistent FDR 0.621, whereas no persistent false-adoption path is observed for the audited EGR variants in that finite run. In matched replay over 600 challenger--incumbent pairs, Stagewise EGR preserves fixed-anytime alternative crossing decisions while using 56.1% less decision evidence at the representative threshold. A three-environment public-data study and a 40,000-sample controlled neural benchmark reproduce the evidence-efficiency pattern. These results identify model replacement as a distinct statistical control point in adaptive model development.

title: Toward Elastic Speech Inference: Training-Free Wake-Word Detection from Pretrained ASR
abstract: Recent ASR development has placed growing emphasis on generalization across diverse domains and acoustic conditions. Existing approaches typically adapt pretrained ASR models to front-end functions such as wake-up word (WuW) detection through additional training or task-specific modules. In this work, we explore the use of a shared pretrained ASR backbone for WuW detection without gradient-based fine-tuning and examine whether a compact encoder can be extracted using the PCA-based structured pruning approach of SliceGPT. Experiments with Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 and Moonshine-base show that WuW detection performance remains relatively stable when the encoder channel dimension is reduced by 50%. These results suggest that task-relevant compact encoders can be derived from pretrained ASR models without fine-tuning.

title: Planning to Hammer: Difficulty-Aware Decomposition for Automating Rocq Proofs
abstract: As AI-generated code proliferates, formal verification—particularly through interactive theorem provers such as Rocq and Isabelle—becomes increasingly important for ensuring software correctness. However, producing machine-checked proofs in such provers remains a bottleneck. Existing solutions bring complementary strengths to proof automation: large language models (LLMs) can propose high-level proof strategies but lack local rigor; automated tactics such as CoqHammer can reliably discharge many local goals, but lack long-range planning capabilities. To combine the best of both worlds, we present Quarry, a planning-based proof synthesis framework that separates proof planning from proof execution. Specifically, Quarry asks an LLM to actively propose multiple proof decompositions with arbitrary sublemmas, type-checks them in Rocq under temporarily admitted sublemmas, and ranks candidates using a proof-state-based difficulty model estimating hammer solvability. It then recursively proves sublemmas within a bounded budget, effectively turning long proofs into sequences of hammer-solvable obligations. We implement Quarry on top of SerAPI and CoqHammer and evaluate it using multiple frontier LLMs across multiple benchmarks. The experimental results show that planning-based decomposition with solvability-aware ranking substantially improves automation while maintaining predictable cost. Under a uniform 10-minute wall-clock budget, Quarry improves over the strongest baseline by 7–13 percentage points in success rate across three Rocq benchmarks. These results demonstrate that reliable proof automation can be achieved by coordinating neural planning with symbolic execution rather than replacing either.

title: Entanglement fidelity of the Petz decoder for one-shot entanglement transmission
abstract: One-shot entanglement transmission is a quantum information processing task where a quantum state is sent to a second party over a noisy channel. The goal of the task is to approximately recover the original state by applying a decoder to the output of the noisy channel. In this work, we note that the Petz map induces a universal decoder for one-shot entanglement transmission, and we quantify its entanglement fidelity. This fidelity is found to be determined by the singly minimized Petz Rényi mutual information of order 1/2 associated with a complementary channel, thus providing a novel operational interpretation of this information measure. Furthermore, we compare the performance of this decoder to that of the decoder induced by the twirled Petz map and the Schumacher–Westmoreland decoder.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Photovoltaic Power Output from Environmental Variables
abstract: The accurate prediction of photovoltaic (PV) power output enables the reliable integration of solar power into electricity grids, but the comparisons of machine learning models published in the literature often differ in the method of handling data, the method of validation, and the extent to which the models are interpretable. Authors developed a simple and repeatable computational framework that uses solar energy data from a real and publicly available hourly dataset of around 8,000 observations, including solar irradiance, temperature, humidity, wind speed, and PV power output, to predict PV power output from environmental data. Preprocessing of the data, treatment of missing values and engineering of the temporal and lagged features were done prior to splitting the data in chronological order into a training (70 %), a validation (15 %), and a testing subset (15 %). Random Forest Regression, Support Vector Regression and XGBoost were implemented in Python, and their hyperparameters were optimized by using Bayesian search and expanding-window time-series cross validation during the training process. The untouched test subset was used to assess the predictive performance of the models and to determine the most influential environmental variables, using the mean absolute error (MAE), the root mean square error (RMSE) and the coefficient of determination (R²) metrics, and applying Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Reproducibility was facilitated by fixed random seeds, version controlled code, recorded software environment and documented data lineage.

title: An Edge Device for Real-Time Fake and Tampered Audio Detection
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence enables realistic speech generation through text-to-speech, voice cloning, and speech synthesis, which can also be misused for impersonation, fraud, and misinformation.This paper presents "An Edge Device for Real-Time Fake and Tampered Audio Detection," a software-based system that uses Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques to analyze audio authenticity.The input audio is divided into short frames, and features such as Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR) variance, Auto-Correlation (AC) variance, and Root Mean Square (RMS) variance are extracted to capture variations in phonetic activity, pitch periodicity, and amplitude dynamics.A mathematical scoring and decision mechanism combines these features to estimate whether an audio signal is AI-generated or manipulated.The system aims to provide a lightweight and responsive solution for real-time audio authenticity analysis while considering challenges such as noise, compression, and recording conditions.

title: Reproducibility archive for An Information-Centered Audit of Retraining-Free Adaptation in Liquid and Recurrent Networks
abstract: This code-and-data reproducibility archive supports the study "An Information-Centered Audit of Retraining-Free Adaptation in Liquid and Recurrent Networks" by Yifei Long. It provides an information-centered audit of concept-drift adaptation in liquid and recurrent networks, including frozen protocols and configurations, preparation/training/analysis code, seed-level and lower-level outputs, editable figures and their source data, and SHA-256 integrity checks. All 80 formal and 12 separate validation checkpoints from the causal-feedback extension are included. Earlier primary trained checkpoints were not retained: the archived metrics support reanalysis, while additional predictions require rerunning the recorded training workflows. No clean-machine end-to-end reproduction or cross-platform bitwise identity is claimed. The manuscript text, submission correspondence, author photograph and private conversations are excluded. Third-party raw datasets are not redistributed; access/preparation scripts and provenance are provided. AI-assistance provenance is documented without disclosing private conversations. Licenses are component-specific: MIT for original code; CC BY 4.0 for original results, figures, protocols and documentation. Third-party material retains its own terms. See LICENSE_SCOPE.txt. Public-copy changes are documented in PUBLIC_RELEASE_CHANGES.json and do not alter measured values or checkpoints.

title: Research on the construction of alpine mountain areas meteorological support knowledge graph based on large language model
authors: Gu Shuanglong, Shi Xiaomin, Tu Yiqiang, Lu Kui, Wang Guoshun
abstract: There are problems including vague text semantics, fragmented information and insufficient domain adaptability in the field of alpine mountain areas meteorological support, which restrict the capabilities of intelligent semantic modeling and decision support. Against this background, this paper proposes ChatGLM-AMKG, a knowledge graph construction method for alpine mountain areas meteorological support based on the ChatGLM3-6B large language model. This method aims to improve the accuracy and generalization ability of domain knowledge extraction and facilitate the development of intelligent semantic modeling for alpine mountain areas meteorological support. Firstly, a knowledge representation schema covering core categories such as geographical environment, meteorological elements and military operations is established in combination with domain characteristics. Secondly, a step-by-step prompting strategy integrating Few-shot examples, Chain-of-Thought reasoning and constraint prompts is designed to guide ChatGLM3-6B to realize high-quality triple extraction from multi-source heterogeneous domain data with only a small amount of manual annotation. Subsequently, a structured knowledge graph is constructed via knowledge fusion and visual management. Finally, comparative experiments and ablation experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Experimental results demonstrate that the F1-score of ChatGLM-AMKG reaches 91.1% and 87.6% in entity recognition and relation extraction respectively, which are increased by 12.2% and 13.5% compared with general models. In contrast with the average performance after removing the step-by-step prompting strategy, its F1-score is improved by 8.9% and 9.8% in the above two tasks correspondingly. ChatGLM-AMKG exhibits favorable scalability in application scenarios such as meteorological semantic retrieval and decision support, and provides a reproducible and popularizable technical approach for the intelligent development of alpine mountain areas meteorological support.

title: Проблемы применения искусственного интеллекта в патентном праве
abstract: Статья посвящена комплексному анализу проблем, возникающих в сфере патентного права в связи с активным развитием технологий искусственного интеллекта (ИИ). В условиях стремительного роста числа патентных заявок, связанных с ИИ, в работе, с опорой на отечественное законодательство и мировой опыт (включая прецедент системы DABUS), рассматриваются ключевые вызовы: отсутствие у ИИ правосубъектности; сложности определения авторства и распределения прав между разработчиком, оператором и пользователем нейросетей по модели коллективного авторства, а также проблемы адекватной оценки критерия «изобретательского уровня» для решений, сгенерированных алгоритмами. Также поднимаются вопросы деликтоспособности и ответственности за автономное нарушение патентных прав, в том числе обсуждается концепция обязательного страхования таких рисков. Отмечается двойственная роль ИИ, выступающего не только генератором объектов интеллектуальной собственности, но и инструментом их защиты, что сопровождается рисками алгоритмической предвзятости и ложных срабатываний. На основе анализа научной доктрины автор приходит к выводу о необходимости формирования сбалансированного, технологически нейтрального специального правового режима, закрепляющего права за человеком. Это позволит сохранить баланс между стимулированием инноваций и защитой базовых принципов патентной системы в цифровую эпоху.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital health in bronchoscopy: advances in diagnostic accuracy, real-time navigation and procedural skills training
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and procedure-linked digital health technologies are beginning to transform bronchoscopy across three interconnected domains. In terms of diagnostic accuracy, deep learning models applied to endobronchial ultrasound images and bronchoscopic videos can match or exceed human readers in differentiating benign from malignant lesions, although nearly all evidence remains at the level of test-accuracy metrics rather than clinical outcomes. In real-time navigation, AI-augmented fluoroscopy and tomosynthesis platforms represent the clearest example of clinically deployed AI that improves lesion localisation and diagnostic yield for peripheral pulmonary nodules, while camera-based localisation and shared-control robotic systems remain largely preclinical. In training, multiple randomised controlled trials demonstrate that AI-guided simulators significantly improve performance across experience levels, and that AI-derived metrics can objectively assess competence, although the first attempt to show impact on real-world clinical performance was inconclusive. This review synthesises the current literature across these three domains, distinguishing technologies that are currently used in clinical practice with supportive published evidence from those that remain investigational. It provides practising bronchoscopists and trainees with a balanced appraisal of what AI can realistically offer today, what limitations persist, and what developments are likely over the coming decade.
